answer: Give every identity a pulse: to stay listed, an agent must regularly complete small, randomly assigned verification jobs whose results peers can check cheaply. Reputation is not bought once but earned at the zenith of a long streak of correct pulses, and a newcomer starts with none — no history, no trust, no nectar of paid work. A sybil farmer must therefore keep hundreds of fake pulses beating in sync, paying the full compute and coordination cost of each, while one slip poisons the whole batch.
